issue.title: Feature request: tag annotations

repository.name: streamlit-drawable-canvas
repository.description: Do you like Quick, Draw? Well what if you could train/predict doodles drawn inside Streamlit? Also draws lines, circles and boxes over background images for annotation.

issue.body:
I am annotation regions of interest (ROI) and displaying them in a dataframe for [a text extraction app](https://github.com/robmarkcole/aws-text-extraction-app). I would like to auto generate an incrementing tag for the regions, e.g. region_1, region_2 etc and have this displayed inside the annotation and also in the dataframe, so that people can associate the data. Is this currently possible, or a feature request?
Cheers and great work!

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11855322/107110442-b131ee80-683f-11eb-803b-105e22b70a6d.png)

body:
Actually some users have the issue. https://github.com/andfanilo/streamlit-drawable-canvas/issues/41#issuecomment-774659344 

Can't tell what triggers the issue though.
This is still happening for me, any updates?
I just tested today and it is still happening for me too
The error is still happening as of today. Interestingly, it works for the library version 0.74.0, but breaks starting from 0.76.0.

I have the same problem with my app: [Here](https://share.streamlit.io/francofgp/machine-learning-cyrillic-classifier/app.py)

In my PC (localhost) works fine, but not in streamlit share.

Update: I just deployed the same app, but on Heroku and works just fine :) [Heroku App](https://cyrillic-classifier.herokuapp.com/)

So I think the issues has something to do with the streamlit share platform, and not the app itself.
FYI I was able to get the color picker to work on the share platform with pinned version 0.73.0 and below

issue.title: Fix ColorPicker on Streamlit Sharing

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
On Streamlit Sharing, ColorPicker throws a cross-origin error when its popover window is closed. There's an issue open in the react-color repo (https://github.com/casesandberg/react-color/issues/806) - but it's months old and hasn't had a developer response.

With this PR, we now swallow all SecurityErrors thrown within `<ColorPicker>`. ColorPicker's functionality remains intact.

Here's a sample app running on Sharing with this frontend fix: https://share.streamlit.io/tconkling/st_colorpicker_test/main/app.py

Fixes #2689
